newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul watchdog finds unfair trade in three stocks.
newsitem.headline: Seoul watchdog finds unfair trade in three stocks.

text.p: South Korea's Securities Supervisory Board said on Friday it had found irregular trading in the shares of Han Mi Pharmaceutical Co, Korea Zinc Co Ltd and Daesung Resources Co.

An official at the securities watchdog said two Han Mi executives violated a securities rule banning insider trading. The two executives bought Han Mi shares from March 13 to 14, 1996, before the company told the Korea Stock Exchange that it had developed an anti-cancer drug, the official said.
Han Mi share prices doubled to 18,000 won in the period, he said.
The board will submit the matter to prosecutors for further investigation and penalties.
A board statement said two brokers at Dongsuh Securities manipulated stock prices of Daesung Resources.
The Dongsuh Securities brokers together bought 57,920 Daesung shares from June to August 1996, and the share prices rose to 141,000 won from 61,800 during that period, a board official said.
Daesung shares shot up last year boosted by a government plan to develop idle mines in Kangwon province into a resort complex. Daesung has substantial real estate holdings in the area.
"We will ask Dongsuh Securities to cut the brokers' wages for more than four months as a penalty," another board official said.
The board also found the honourary chairman of Youngpoong Group, helped by a broker at Tongyang Securities, manipulated prices of Korea Zinc from April to May 1996.
Korea Zinc share prices rose to 21,000 won from 17,200 during the period.

The board said that because of the Youngpoong chairman's age, 87, it would only warn him not to engage further in price manipulation. But the salary of the Tongyang Securities broker will be reduced for at least four months.
